newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks open second half of 1996/97 bit lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks open second half of 1996/97 bit lower.

text.p: Tokyo stocks kicked off the second half of the 1996/97 financial year slightly lower on Tuesday.
The market's benchmark Nikkei average lost its upward momentum after rallying for five consecutive trading days, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average dropped 54.20 points or 0.25 percent at 21,502.20 in the first eight minutes of trade. In the futures market, the key September futures had fallen 30 points to 21,540.
"The Nikkei is likely to consolidate around 21,500, as institutional investors are not expected to buy actively," said an analyst at a Japanese securities house.
Brokers said the market was lacking factors to inspire institutional investors to chase higher price levels.

Koichi Ayabe, general manager at Hinode Securities, said stock prices tend to be capped by profit taking when stocks close higher on the day of corporate book closings. Monday was the last day of the first half of the 1996/97 business year for many Japanese companies.
He added that the upside of the stock market could be limited for a while.
